parties.petitioner: Sanjeet Kumar Singh @ Munna Kumar Singh

summary: Appellant challenged conviction under Section 20(b)(ii)(C) of NDPS Act for possession of 47.370 kg ganja recovered from car dickey, confirmed by High Court. Prosecution relied on testimony of DSP (PW-7) as informant and IO, supported by procedural compliance under Sections 42, 43, 49, 50 NDPS Act. Independent witnesses (CW-1, CW-2) denied presence, creating non-corroboration. Co-accused Reena Das acquitted due to lack of evidence linking her to contraband. Appellant argued bias from informant-IO overlap, lack of corroboration, and inconsistent documents. State contended procedural compliance, irrelevance of Section 50 for vehicle search, and presumption of guilt under Section 54. Courts below upheld conviction based on DSP's credible testimony and documentary consistency. Issue: whether lack of independent witness corroboration and procedural discrepancies vitiate conviction.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 20(b)(ii)(C) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
Ajmer Singh vs. State of Haryana

final_judgment: Appeal dismissed. Conviction and sentence of 10 years rigorous imprisonment with Rs.1 lakh fine upheld. Concurrent findings of Special Court and High Court sustained based on credible testimony of PW-7 and compliance with mandatory procedures under NDPS Act, despite hostile independent witnesses.
